answer: Identity minting costs a stake bond plus a per-period fee that rises with issuance rate, like a tide; bonds are scored by independent oracles and labeled by risk tiers (opal, saffron). Rewards use a concave function, e.g. sqrt(stake×reputation), so splitting stake s into N IDs gives Σsqrt(s_i)≤sqrt(s), never more reward. Attacker pays N bonds, N fees, and oracle-evidence costs; issuance is throttled. Limitation: colluding real agents and oracle capture can still Sybil, and concave rewards cap honest scaling.
